The test is whether your usual place of abode is outside the UK, which HMRC treats as met once you are abroad for six months or more, even if you remain UK tax resident under the Statutory Residence Test. HMRC's guidance at PIM4850 covers exactly this trap, and it catches people every year.

intro: If your usual home is outside the UK, we manage your Nottingham property for a £600 setup fee, then 12% of the rent, including any VAT, on a fully managed basis only. blocks.text: Letting agents of non-resident landlords must register with HMRC and, unless HMRC approves gross payment, deduct basic rate tax from the net rent each quarter and account for it. There is no minimum rent below which this disappears: where an agent is involved, the scheme applies from the first pound, under HMRC's own guidance at PIM4810. And the test is your usual place of abode, not your tax residence, so it can catch people who still count as UK resident under the Statutory Residence Test, per PIM4850.

Inside the 12% we register, calculate, file the annual return and issue your NRL6 certificate by 5 July each year, so your own tax return has the paper it needs. Each quarterly HMRC submission is charged at £60. If you want to receive rent gross, we guide you through the NRL1 application, and once HMRC approves, we pay gross and the quarterly deductions stop.

Nottingham City Council's selective and additional licensing schemes expect a licence holder who can actually be reached: in practice the holder must usually reside in the UK or be a UK registered company. A landlord in Dubai or Toronto cannot sensibly hold one. Where your property needs a licence, we act as the named holder under a written agreement Trent Law Solicitors has drafted, and that standing is included in the 12% rather than sold as an extra. Handling the licence application itself is £240 for a selective licence or £280 for an HMO licence; the council charges its own application fee on top, and we tell you that figure for your address before anything is submitted.

Whether you need a licence at all depends on which council governs your street, not on the word Nottingham in the address: West Bridgford, for instance, sits in Rushcliffe, which runs no selective or additional scheme at all, checked August 2026. faqs.a: Traditional auction exchanges contracts on the fall of the hammer, with a deposit that day and completion typically 28 days later. The traditional, unconditional method: the winning bid is an exchange of contracts there and then, the buyer pays a deposit, normally 10%, on the day, and completion follows on a fixed date, typically 28 days later. It is the strongest form of certainty a seller can buy, which is why lenders, executors and landlords selling tenanted stock favour it. The price discovery is honest too: competitive bidding in the open, against a reserve you set and we agree together.

sections.heading: Traditional auction: exchange on the fall of the hammer

blocks.text: The conditional method gives the winning bidder a reservation period, commonly 28 days to exchange and a further 28 to complete, in return for a non-refundable reservation fee. It opens the auction to mortgage buyers, who need time a traditional auction does not give, which usually widens the field for ordinary residential stock. The trade is a longer timetable and a result that is binding in practice but not an instant exchange. The detail varies by platform, which is exactly why the written note comes first.

Serious bidders read the legal pack before the auction, and a thin pack costs money: every unanswered question becomes a discount in someone's bidding limit. Trent Law Solicitors prepares ours, title, searches, replies to enquiries, tenancy and licensing papers where they apply, so bidders can commit without fear.
